newsitem.title: IRAQ: U.N. arms official discusses inspections with Iraq.
newsitem.headline: U.N. arms official discusses inspections with Iraq.

text.p: A senior U.N. arms official has discussed Iraq's obstruction of U.N. inspections with an adviser to President Saddam Hussein, a U.N. spokeswoman said on Sunday.

Jo Lomas said Charles Deulfer, deputy chairman of the U.N. Special Commission (UNSCOM) overseeing elimination of Iraq's prohibited weapons, "discussed recent sensitivities between UNSCOM and Iraq" with Presidential Adviser Amir al-Sa'di.
"They had a long non-confrontational meeting," Lomas told Reuters.
Duelfer, who arrived in Baghdad on Saturday after Iraq prevented arms inspection teams from entering three sites this month, is scheduled to meet al-Sa'di again before leaving on Tuesday.

Rolf Ekeus, the chairman of UNSCOM, complained to the U.N. Security Council that Baghdad had prevented U.N. inspectors from entering sites and endangered U.N. helicopters and their crews assisting U.N. ground teams.
Late on Saturday, the United Nations Security Council responded by unanimously warning Iraq it faced further sanctions if it obstructed U.N. inspectors.

UNSCOM must certify Iraq has no weapons of mass destruction before the United Nations will lift curbs on its oil exports. The U.N. has allowed Baghdad since December to sell $2 billion worth of oil to buy urgently needed goods.
The sanctions were imposed following Iraq's 1990 invasion of Kuwait.

The government newspaper al-Jumhouriya said Iraq's former culture and information minister Abdul-al-Ghani Abdul-al-Ghafur urged the United Nations Security Council to put Ekeus on trial because inspectors examined religious sites in Baghdad last week for hidden weapons.
Iraq said on Wednesday an UNSCOM arms team inspected a church and two convents on the outskirts of Baghdad.
